mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for four consecutive weeks (-90.3 to -82.9). This momentum reflects entrenched behavioral habituation to increased outings, which should persist and push the next 4-week mean higher than the last 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact: four consecutive weekly increases from -90.3 to -82.9
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the uptrend continuing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved by more than 5 points per week for two consecutive weeks (-79.3 to -68.3), indicating active policy relaxation of workplace restrictions. This loosening directly enables ancillary retail trips during commutes, raising RETAIL_REC within 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES rose from -79.3 to -68.3 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues improving by more than 5 points per week but RETAIL_REC growth decelerates or reverses over the next 2 weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility (both improving each week) interacts to amplify retail footfall beyond what either series alone would predict, since commuters combine transit-enabled trips with shopping stops, driving RETAIL_REC higher over 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT rose from -83.4 to -74.1 while WORKPLACES rose from -79.3 to -68.3
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both continue rising by more than 5 points weekly but RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean does not exceed the prior 4-week mean, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 33.4 to 29.0, indicating people are spending progressively less time at home. This freed behavioral capacity is redirected toward discretionary outings, raising RETAIL_REC over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL declined from 33.4 to 29.0 over four weeks
regime_hint: reopening phase with declining residential confinement
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility improved from -98.0 to -94.7, reflecting seasonal or weather-driven resumption of outdoor activity. This short-term outdoor activity resurgence typically coincides with nearby retail and recreation visits within one week.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS improved from -98.0 to -94.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS continues improving but RETAIL_REC shows no increase in the immediate following week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has crossed above -55 (rising from -68.0 to -53.0), signaling a behavioral shift away from essential-only shopping mode. This relaxation of restrictive shopping habits extends to non-essential retail, boosting RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM rose from -68.0 to -53.0, crossing -55 in the latest week
regime_hint: transition from essential-only to broader shopping behavior
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above -55 but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in RESIDENTIAL alongside rising WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects a systemic, policy-driven unlock of mobility restrictions across multiple domains simultaneously. This compound easing compounds into sustained RETAIL_REC growth over a full month.
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES, TRANSIT rose and RESIDENTIAL fell concurrently over four weeks
failure_condition: If all three indicators continue trending as described for 4 weeks but RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean does not exceed the prior 4-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-peak lockdown recovery regime, PARKS mobility crossing above -95 marks entry into a seasonal outdoor-activity window that historically sustains elevated retail and recreation engagement for a full month once outdoor access normalizes.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS improved from -98.0 to -94.7, crossing -95 in the latest week
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above -95 for the next 4 weeks but RETAIL_REC's 4-week average does not rise relative to the prior period, the hypothesis is rejected.
